title: Stream synchronization, kernel-fit scoring, and graph reconciliation
creator: Aisha Menon
description:
Objective: Reduce rare decode-time correctness failures and intermittent latency spikes observed when multiple decode streams share CUDA Graphs. Deliver a lightweight kernel-fit scoring layer + epoch reconciliation protocol that avoids expensive full recapture while ensuring deterministic replay for the common failure modes.

Acceptance criteria:
- <5% repro rate on synthetic cross-stream interleave fuzz suite for 48-hour soak compared to baseline.
- No >5% p99 latency regression on steady-state throughput tests.
- Automated CI job that validates determinism for 3 representative model families (gpt-3-like, llama2-like, and long-seq transformer).
- Rollout plan with canary and automatic fallback to per-request kernel binding when a mismatch is detected.
comments: 2026-02-19: Kickoff meeting notes: walking through production incidents where multi-stream decodes triggered graph replay divergence. Agreed to split work into two deliverables: (A) kernel-fit scorer that selects compatible kernel candidates without recapturing, (B) epoch reconciliation that verifies token-alignment and performs minimal recovery when divergence detected. See design sketch: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/STREAM-SYNC-DESIGN

2026-02-24: Prototype: implemented kernel-fit scoring heuristic based on (i) current occupancy, (ii) quantization fingerprint, and (iii) sequence-length distribution hash. Early microbenchmarks show 12% reduction in unnecessary recaptures on ci-small. Benchmark notebook: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A_kernel_fit_prototype

2026-03-01: Trade-offs discussion with runtime team: scoring needs to be fast (<=200us) to avoid adding latency to prefill path. Decided against full model-parameter checksum due to HSM/KMS overheads in Private mode; instead use a compact model-layout fingerprint + kernel ABI version number. Carlos requested an escape hatch to force per-request binding via environment flag REDWOOD_FORCE_BINDING=true for investigation in prod.

2026-03-03: Interop feedback from quantization team: certain int8 kernels use implicit reorder steps that break the simple fingerprint. Action: extend fingerprint to include reorder-tag and micro-op count. Added label 'quant-signal' to captures for richer matching. See PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2543

2026-03-06: Testing update: ran fuzz harness across 3 node types (A100, H100, L4) with 24h mixed load. Observed 0.9% deterministic mismatch rate concentrated on long-seq workloads (>4k tokens) using mixed-quant models. Plan: add epochal KV fence that inserts lightweight alignment checkpoints after prefill segments >512 tokens to bound KV drift.

2026-03-09: Review notes from SRE (Janelle Wu): favor non-disruptive rollout — canary on dedicated pool with circuit-breaker for >0.2% mismatch. Also requested Datadog metrics: runtime.kernel_fit.score, runtime.epoch_reconcile.invocations, runtime.replay_fallback.count. Dashboards: https://app.datadoghq.com/dashboard/RTS-graph-replay

2026-03-11: Implementation status: kernel-fit scorer merged to feature branch, reconciliation harness implemented behind runtime flag --enable-epoch-reconcile. Added deterministic smoke tests to CI that replay golden traces; initial green except for one flaky trace (investigating). Next: harden alignment fence codepath and prepare canary run for week of 2026-03-22. Linked PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2561 https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2569

Notes for rollout: 1) Enable on a small percentage of Dedicated pools, 2) monitor replay_fallback.count and p99 latency, 3) if fallback increases above threshold, automatically throttle to zero and create incident. Added runbook stub: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SRE/pages/GRAPH-RECONCILE-RUNBOOK
